title: Clearing denominators in a residue-field minimal polynomial
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $\mathfrak p\subset R$ a prime, and $L/\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ a finite separable field extension [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. If $\alpha\in L$ generates $L$ over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, then there are $c\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$ and a monic polynomial $f\in R[T]$ such that the image of $f$ in $\kappa(\mathfrak p)[T]$ is the minimal polynomial of the image of $c\alpha$ over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00UD (algebra-lemma-make-etale-map-prescribed-residue-field), lines 39819-39835: after replacing alpha by c alpha with c not in p, coefficients of the minimal polynomial lift from R

proof.text: Write $\kappa=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $\pi:R\to\kappa$ for the canonical map $r\mapsto r/1\bmod\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}$; for $r\in R$ write $r\alpha$ for $\pi(r)\alpha\in L$. Since $L/\kappa$ is separable algebraic, $\alpha$ is algebraic over $\kappa$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension], so it has a minimal polynomial $g=P_\alpha=T^d+a_{d-1}T^{d-1}+\dots+a_0\in\kappa[T]$, monic of degree $d\geq1$, with $g(\alpha)=0$, and every nonzero $q\in\kappa[T]$ with $q(\alpha)=0$ has $\deg q\geq d$ (definition of $P_\alpha$ as the monic polynomial of least degree vanishing at $\alpha$).

proof.text: The minimal polynomial of $\beta=c\alpha=\gamma\alpha$. Let $h=T^d+\gamma a_{d-1}T^{d-1}+\gamma^2a_{d-2}T^{d-2}+\dots+\gamma^da_0=\gamma^dg(T/\gamma)\in\kappa[T]$. It is monic of degree $d$, and $h(\beta)=\gamma^dg(\alpha)=0$. If $q\in\kappa[T]$ is nonzero with $q(\beta)=0$, then $q(\gamma T)$ has the same degree as $q$ (its leading coefficient is that of $q$ times $\gamma^{\deg q}\neq0$, $\kappa$ a field) and vanishes at $\alpha$, so $\deg q\geq d$ by step 1. Hence $h$ is a monic polynomial of least degree vanishing at $\beta$; it is the only one, since the difference of two such is zero or a nonzero polynomial of smaller degree vanishing at $\beta$. So $h=P_\beta$ is the minimal polynomial of $\beta$ over $\kappa$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. (As $\gamma\in\kappa^\times$, also $\kappa(\beta)=\kappa(\alpha)=L$, which the citing proof uses.)

proof.text: Lift. Let $f=T^d+r_{d-1}T^{d-1}+\dots+r_0\in R[T]$ with the $r_i$ of step 2; $f$ is monic, and applying $\pi$ to its coefficients gives $T^d+\sum_{i<d}\gamma^{d-i}a_iT^i=h$ by step 2. By step 3 the image of $f$ in $\kappa(\mathfrak p)[T]$ is the minimal polynomial of the image of $c\alpha$, with $c\in R\setminus\mathfrak p$.
